objective.description: Define and implement the single client-agnostic path by which local coding agents discover a workspace identity and a global local Throughline daemon routes every MCP operation to its logical persistence scope.

objective.title: Enable deterministic Throughline workspace routing

alternatives: Bind one MCP process to one workspace from its startup directory.
Configure a separate MCP entry for every workspace.
Accept arbitrary filesystem or database paths in tool calls.
decisions.outcome: Throughline exposes one client-agnostic MCP contract in which every operation is scoped by a stable workspace_id. The server resolves that identifier through an allowlisted workspace registry. Correct routing must not depend on a client starting one MCP process per task, inheriting a particular working directory, or exposing a client-specific environment variable.
decisions.rationale: MCP clients control process and connection lifecycles differently. An explicit workspace identity works across Codex, Claude Code, Hermes, and future clients. It also keeps workspace identity separate from physical storage topology.
decisions.title: Use explicit logical workspace routing

alternatives: Infer a workspace from the MCP process working directory or environment.
Bind mutable workspace state to an MCP connection.
Store workspace identifiers in provider-specific instruction files.
decisions.outcome: Throughline uses exactly one workspace bootstrap and routing path. throughline init writes a stable workspace_id to the canonical .throughline/config.toml and registers that identifier in the allowlisted global workspace registry. Before its first Throughline tool call, an agent deterministically searches upward from the task working directory for the nearest .throughline/config.toml, reads workspace_id, and includes it explicitly in every MCP operation. Every tool requires workspace_id; missing or unknown identifiers fail closed. There is no local default, server-side working-directory inference, environment-variable routing, connection-level bind_workspace state, client-specific adapter, or duplicated workspace identifier in AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, or equivalent files. MCP server instructions and tool descriptions define this bootstrap procedure.
decisions.rationale: A single canonical source, discovery algorithm, and request-level routing contract prevents ambiguous behavior and configuration drift across Codex, Claude Code, Hermes, parallel agent graphs, and future MCP clients. Explicit request scoping also remains correct when clients reuse or recreate processes and connections differently.
decisions.title: Use one canonical file-based workspace routing path

alternatives: Require workspace-scoped cryptographic capabilities for every agent from the first milestone.
Treat workspace_id or actor_id as an authentication credential.
Expose the daemon beyond the local user boundary.
decisions.outcome: The initial Throughline multi-workspace routing milestone coordinates cooperative agents running under the same local user account. workspace_id, actor_id, claims, optimistic versions, and idempotency keys provide deterministic routing, attribution, and concurrency safety; they are not treated as cryptographic authentication or adversarial tenant-isolation boundaries. The global Throughline daemon must remain local-only, fail closed for missing or unknown workspace identifiers, and never accept arbitrary storage paths. Strict isolation between mutually untrusted agents or workspaces is explicitly outside this milestone and requires a future authorization design.
decisions.rationale: The immediate goal is reliable coordination among trusted local coding agents across Codex, Claude Code, Hermes, and similar harnesses. Introducing per-agent capabilities or adversarial multi-tenant authorization now would add substantial complexity without serving the current use case. Recording the boundary prevents coordination identities from being misrepresented as security principals.
decisions.title: Adopt a cooperative local-agent threat model for the initial milestone

decisions.outcome: Throughline exposes exactly one MCP transport: Streamable HTTP on a per-user loopback endpoint. One independently managed Throughline daemon accepts concurrent connections from globally configured Codex, Claude Code, and Hermes clients. Each request remains independently routable and every workspace-scoped tool requires workspace_id. Bind only to loopback, validate Origin, and require bearer authentication. Do not ship STDIO or legacy SSE as alternative product paths. Workspace discovery guidance is authoritative in relevant tool schemas and descriptions because server instructions are not portable across all supported harnesses.
decisions.title: Use one loopback Streamable HTTP transport

decisions.outcome: A one-time idempotent throughline setup command creates protected per-user configuration and credentials, persists the loopback endpoint, installs and starts exactly one OS-managed user daemon, and atomically reconciles global MCP entries for detected supported harnesses without blindly overwriting conflicts. Per-workspace throughline init only initializes workspace identity and registration. throughline daemon status, start, stop, restart, and logs always control that same OS-managed service and never spawn an alternative server. launchd and systemd --user are adapters behind one daemon-management seam; Throughline does not implement its own process supervisor. The service auto-starts and crash-restarts. Authenticated health reports version, registry state, and provider readiness. Updates replace the binary and restart the same service while preserving credentials, registry, and workspace data. Uninstall removes the service and managed global MCP entries but preserves workspace data unless explicit purge is requested. The legacy public throughline mcp STDIO path is removed through the migration path.
decisions.title: Use one managed per-user daemon lifecycle

decisions.outcome: throughline setup generates one cryptographically random 256-bit bearer token per local user and writes the same token as a static Authorization header into managed global Codex, Claude Code, and Hermes configurations. Throughline credential and managed client configuration files must be user-readable only. Environment variables, OAuth, TLS, OS keychains, per-agent credentials, and alternate transports are not the V1 default. The daemon binds only to 127.0.0.1, validates Host and Origin, permits absent Origin for native MCP clients, rejects foreign browser origins, exposes no CORS, and authenticates before MCP parsing or workspace routing. Health is authenticated. All endpoints enforce body limits and timeouts; logs redact credentials and storage details. Unknown workspace IDs fail generically without revealing paths or providers. Tokens never enter workspace configuration, registry data, databases, logs, status output, or errors. Rotation preflights every managed target, creates backups, updates credentials and client configurations, restarts the same service, and rolls back on failure. Cooperative agents under one OS user share the token; actor IDs, claims, versions, and idempotency are coordination rather than authentication. Malicious processes running as that same OS user remain outside the V1 threat model.
decisions.title: Protect the local daemon with one per-user bearer credential

decisions.outcome: workspace_id identifies one logical workspace, not one directory path. Moving or renaming a workspace preserves its identity; idempotent throughline init updates the registry when the previous canonical path no longer exists. A copied directory that includes .throughline/config.toml initially represents the same logical workspace. Creating an independent copy requires throughline init --fork before use; it creates a new workspace_id while retaining history with explicit fork provenance. Normal Git clones receive new identities because .throughline remains ignored. If two existing canonical paths claim the same ID, registration fails closed with workspace_identity_conflict and never silently reassigns identity. Normal re-init never changes the ID. Upward discovery selects the nearest config, allowing explicit nested workspaces. Registry paths are physically canonicalized so symlinks do not create another identity. Missing or deleted workspaces become unavailable; IDs are never automatically deleted, reused, or reinitialized. Removal and destructive reinitialization require explicit commands and cannot silently delete history. ID-only routing cannot reliably distinguish a move from a copy, so independent copies require an explicit fork rather than heuristic auto-detection.
decisions.title: Treat workspace identity as logical identity rather than path identity

decisions.outcome: Throughline will not implement automatic workspace migration, lazy migration, STDIO compatibility, dual runtime paths, or rollback machinery for the current two disposable test workspaces. Before cutover, export the current OBJ-WORKSPACE-ROUTING objective and accepted context to an English Markdown artifact. Archive rather than immediately delete each legacy .throughline directory, remove legacy STDIO client configuration, install and run throughline setup, initialize each repository afresh with throughline init, recreate the routing objective in the new workspace, verify the new daemon path, and only then delete the archives. New Throughline versions fail closed on legacy workspace configuration with legacy_workspace_unsupported and provide explicit export, archive, reset, and reinitialize instructions. Legacy throughline mcp does not remain as a functioning compatibility path. This is a deliberate pre-product clean cut justified by having only two test workspaces.
decisions.title: Use a clean cut instead of product migration support

decisions.outcome: Throughline stores one administrative workspace registry in the platform user-state directory: ~/Library/Application Support/Throughline/registry.db on macOS and ${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/throughline/registry.db on Linux. The directory is mode 0700 and the database is mode 0600. Tests inject a temporary registry path; production has no alternate registry-location routing mechanism. The registry is not a workspace persistence provider. It maps workspace_id to a provider-neutral WorkspaceTarget containing provider kind, an opaque non-secret provider locator, canonical physical workspace root, config fingerprint, lifecycle state, generation, and audit timestamps. It never stores bearer credentials or provider secrets. Only administrative CLI flows such as setup, init, fork, relocate, and unregister mutate it through SQLite transactions and optimistic generation checks. Fresh init uses a recoverable pending-to-active registration around atomic fsync-and-rename config creation; only active entries are routable. The daemon performs a read-only registry lookup for every workspace-scoped request, so changes require no reload, cache invalidation, or connection-bound state. It validates the active entry, config fingerprint, canonical root, and provider target availability before handing the opaque target to the persistence-provider layer. Unknown IDs return workspace_not_found; missing roots or targets return workspace_unavailable; disagreement returns workspace_registry_conflict. No request may supply or override a path or provider locator. Move reconciliation is allowed only when the former canonical root is unavailable; simultaneous roots with one ID fail closed. Unregistering removes routing authority but preserves provider data unless an explicit purge is separately confirmed. The registry seam replaces the current CLI coupling from workspace discovery directly to SQLite Open; all domain-facing MCP and CLI calls route through it.
decisions.title: Use one per-user SQLite registry as the exclusive routing allowlist

decisions.outcome: The daemon exposes one deep internal WorkspaceRouter interface to the MCP adapter: resolve a required workspace_id to an application Service for the current request. The router resolves an active WorkspaceTarget through the registry, then delegates the target to a ProviderManager. WorkspaceTarget contains workspace identity, provider kind, opaque non-secret locator, and registry generation; neither the router nor domain interprets provider locators. ProviderManager selects a PersistenceProvider adapter by provider kind. A provider owns its connection topology and returns a ports.Store for the target; it may use one SQLite database per workspace, one shared Postgres pool with tenant or schema routing, or another strategy. No layer above the provider assumes workspace equals database or connection. The router constructs or reuses app.Service with the returned store plus shared ID generator and clock. Runtime entries are keyed by workspace_id and target generation; concurrent cache misses are single-flight, generation changes replace the runtime after in-flight work drains, idle runtimes may be bounded and evicted, and daemon shutdown drains and closes providers. Failure to open one target is isolated and never poisons other workspaces. The SQLite provider owns one configured database handle per active SQLite target, preserving its explicit writer boundary while allowing different workspaces to execute independently. A fake shared provider must prove that multiple WorkspaceTargets can share one provider instance without cross-workspace leakage. The MCP server is constructed with WorkspaceRouter rather than one app.Service, and one central request wrapper validates required workspace_id and resolves the service before invoking a tool handler; no handler, connection, context default, domain command, or client may select a workspace by path. Domain-facing CLI commands remain daemon clients and never instantiate providers directly. Provider secrets stay in provider-owned configuration and never enter WorkspaceTarget, the registry response, MCP output, or logs.
decisions.title: Route workspace requests through a provider-neutral runtime manager

decisions.outcome: Authentication and transport rejection happen before MCP parsing: missing or invalid bearer credentials return HTTP 401, rejected Host or Origin returns HTTP 403, and neither response reveals workspace state. Workspace-scoped tool failures use one structured error envelope with stable code, safe message, retryable boolean, request_id, and optional non-secret remediation code. Initial routing codes are workspace_required, workspace_invalid, workspace_not_found, workspace_pending, workspace_unavailable, workspace_registry_conflict, provider_unsupported, provider_unavailable, and workspace_busy. Errors never include filesystem paths, provider locators, credentials, DSNs, SQL, or cross-workspace details. throughline doctor is the single read-only diagnostic command: it checks service installation and version, authenticated health, managed harness configuration, nearest workspace config, registry agreement, and provider readiness, then points only to the authoritative setup or init remediation path; it never repairs or creates a second route. throughline daemon status --json exposes stable machine-readable service and health state. Authenticated health remains minimal. Logs use request_id and opaque workspace_id with result code and timing while redacting headers, paths, locators, payload secrets, and storage errors. No routing error silently falls back to another workspace, provider, transport, CWD, or connection state.
decisions.title: Expose stable fail-closed routing diagnostics

decisions.outcome: Throughline remains coordination state rather than an execution harness and does not add an agent-graph domain model. At graph-run bootstrap, the orchestrator generates a UUIDv7 run_id. Every logical node uses a distinct stable actor_id formatted agent:<harness>:<run_id>:<node_key>, registers it as kind agent, and reuses it only when resuming that same logical node. Harness task IDs may be recorded as metadata but are not required because no portable provider-wide task identifier exists. Parallel nodes share workspace_id and objective or plan identifiers but never share actor_id, claim ownership, or idempotency keys. Each logical mutation uses an idempotency key derived from run_id, node_key, operation, logical target, and attempt; an exact transport retry reuses the identical key and payload, while a new semantic attempt uses a new attempt suffix. Request correlation IDs are separate from idempotency. Generic actor IDs such as agent:codex are not valid for parallel execution. Claims, leases, optimistic versions, dependencies, and idempotency remain the conflict controls: a version conflict requires rereading authoritative state rather than blindly changing expected_version, and a crashed node resumes with its actor identity or lets the claim expire. Actor identity is not authentication, does not imply an authority principal, and is never derived from the shared bearer credential or MCP connection.
decisions.title: Give every parallel graph node a distinct logical actor identity

decisions.outcome: Remove the hard dependency edge WR-02 -> WR-01 (kind: hard) and replace it with a soft dependency for traceability. WR-01's actual deliverable (docs/product/workspace-routing-spec.md) is verified complete and its acceptance criteria are individually resolved via patch_item.acceptance_criterion_resolutions; WR-01 cannot reach execution_status done only because an accidentally-created, permanently unsatisfiable expected_output (caused by a client-side MCP tool-arg encoding defect for untyped-schema parameters, see recorded risk 01a03939-fb2c-721b-86a5-e8abf673abe9) blocks the review->done transition, which in turn blocks claim_item on every downstream work item via the hard-dependency gate. The user was asked and explicitly approved removing this one edge rather than stalling the whole graph.
decisions.rationale: This is a workaround for broken Throughline/environment tooling, not a scope or architecture change: WR-01's content and sequencing intent are unaffected. Re-link as hard once the daemon rebuild in WR-04/06 replaces the currently-connected legacy MCP server and the encoding defect no longer applies, or once an expected-output removal path exists.

selected_context.body: A workspace_id identifies a logical Throughline scope, not a database instance. Workspace resolution must produce a provider-neutral persistence target. Each persistence provider owns the physical mapping: the SQLite provider may map a workspace to a dedicated file, while a PostgreSQL provider may multiplex many workspaces through one database or connection pool and isolate them by tenant key, schema, row-level scope, or another provider-specific strategy. MCP routing and domain services must not assume one workspace equals one database. The concrete provider abstraction is deferred until another persistence provider is implemented, but the routing contract must preserve this boundary now.
selected_context.title: Workspace identity is a logical persistence scope

selected_context.body: throughline init must idempotently create a stable workspace_id in the canonical .throughline/config.toml and atomically register the workspace in the per-user allowlisted registry. It must reject identifier collisions and silent rebinding.
selected_context.title: Initialization creates one durable workspace identity

selected_context.body: Every Throughline MCP tool must require workspace_id. The router must resolve it before accessing domain or persistence services and must fail closed with stable machine-readable errors when the identifier is missing, unknown, conflicting, or unavailable.
selected_context.title: Every MCP operation is explicitly workspace-scoped

selected_context.body: Codex, Claude Code, Hermes, and each other explicitly supported local coding harness must connect through one canonical global MCP configuration to the same per-user Throughline daemon, without repository-specific MCP entries or a fallback transport.
selected_context.title: Supported harnesses share one local daemon

selected_context.body: Workspace routing must resolve workspace_id to a provider-neutral logical persistence target. Domain and MCP layers must not assume one workspace equals one database, file, schema, connection, or process.
selected_context.title: Routing remains independent of physical storage topology

selected_context.body: Concurrent requests for the same or different workspaces must not share mutable workspace-selection state. Existing optimistic versions, idempotency, claims, leases, and transactions must remain effective, and one unavailable or corrupt workspace must not terminate the daemon or affect another workspace.
selected_context.title: Parallel requests remain isolated and recoverable

selected_context.body: Every request and resulting activity must be attributable to workspace_id and actor_id. Diagnostics must expose stable routing outcomes and error codes while avoiding database paths, credentials, authorization tokens, or unrelated workspace metadata.
selected_context.title: Routing is traceable without leaking storage details

selected_context.body: Each supported local coding harness gives its agent a deterministic task working directory and permission to read the nearest .throughline/config.toml before the first Throughline MCP call.
selected_context.title: Supported harnesses expose the task workspace

selected_context.body: Codex, Claude Code, and Hermes can each globally configure the same local long-lived MCP transport and endpoint without requiring a repository-specific launcher.
selected_context.title: Target harnesses support one common daemon transport

selected_context.body: Any omitted workspace predicate, incorrectly keyed cache, mutable current-workspace state, or provider context leak could route reads or writes to the wrong logical workspace.
selected_context.title: Incorrect scoping could leak or mutate another workspace

selected_context.body: Interrupted initialization, concurrent registration, moved or copied workspaces, stale daemon state, and identifier reuse can create conflicting mappings unless registry updates and lifecycle operations are explicit and atomic.
selected_context.title: Registry and workspace configuration can diverge

selected_context.body: A crash, leaked handle, migration failure, or unbounded resource use in one workspace could affect all connected tasks unless provider handles, errors, and lifecycle operations are isolated per workspace.
selected_context.title: A global daemon can amplify failures

selected_context.body: WAL and busy timeouts preserve correctness but do not remove the single-writer boundary. Bursty parallel graph nodes may cause latency or timeout failures and require bounded retry, short transactions, and load tests.
selected_context.title: Parallel agent graphs can exhaust SQLite write capacity

selected_context.body: If any target harness cannot connect to the selected daemon transport or does not surface MCP instructions consistently, adding a client-specific fallback would violate the accepted architecture.
selected_context.title: Harness transport differences can break the single-path goal

selected_context.body: Current supported versions of Codex, Claude Code, and Hermes each connect through their one global configuration to the same local daemon and successfully call Throughline for a workspace without repository-specific MCP configuration.
selected_context.title: Target harnesses use the same daemon contract

selected_context.body: From the workspace root and nested directories, an agent selects the nearest initialized .throughline/config.toml and sends its stable workspace_id. Missing, unknown, conflicting, and unavailable identifiers produce the specified machine-readable errors without fallback.
selected_context.title: Workspace bootstrap is deterministic and fail-closed

selected_context.body: Parallel reads and mutations against at least two registered workspaces through one daemon never return, modify, cache, or log data under the wrong workspace identity.
selected_context.title: Concurrent workspaces remain isolated

selected_context.body: Initialization is idempotent, concurrent registration cannot corrupt the registry, identifier collisions and silent rebinding are rejected, and newly registered workspaces become routable through the documented single lifecycle without partial state.
selected_context.title: Workspace registration is durable and atomic

selected_context.body: Multiple graph nodes using distinct actor and idempotency identities can execute independent work concurrently; two nodes cannot hold an active claim on the same work item, and version conflicts never cause lost updates.
selected_context.title: Parallel agent graphs preserve coordination guarantees

selected_context.body: Contract tests route multiple workspace_ids through a fake shared persistence provider without changing MCP or domain-service semantics and without assuming a database instance per workspace.
selected_context.title: Routing is demonstrably provider-neutral

selected_context.body: An unavailable, corrupt, or migration-failing workspace returns a scoped error while healthy registered workspaces continue serving requests; daemon restart preserves registry identity and routing behavior.
selected_context.title: One workspace failure does not disable the daemon

selected_context.body: Codex 0.149.1, Claude Code 2.1.231, and Hermes Agent 0.19.0 can each use a user-level MCP configuration to connect to one independently managed loopback Streamable HTTP daemon and send bearer authentication. Global configuration does not imply a shared connection; each task or process may establish its own MCP session.
selected_context.title: Streamable HTTP is the common transport

Workspace discovery guidance must therefore be carried by every relevant tool schema or description, while workspace_id remains a required request argument.
selected_context.title: MCP server instructions are not portable across target harnesses

selected_context.body: On the currently running legacy Throughline MCP: (1) list_output_profiles fails with output_validation_failed: "output.result[0].semantics has unknown field capabilities_do_not_grant_authority" — no output profile can be listed or selected, so define_expected_output/create_output_revision/record_validation (which requires output_revision_id) cannot be completed for any work item right now. (2) append_progress rejects any non-empty completed/remaining array with "json: cannot unmarshal string into Go struct field progressInput.completed of type []string" even when a proper JSON array is sent, so only summary-only progress calls succeed. Worked around by completing WR-01 via a direct transition_item to done and recording evidence via attach_artifact only. These are legacy-server defects unrelated to WR-01..WR-15 scope; do not fix them as part of this objective, but they affect how work-item completion is recorded until the new daemon replaces this instance.
selected_context.title: Two live Throughline MCP defects block output-profile and progress-array flows

selected_context.body:
Root cause identified: my MCP tool-calling environment serializes non-scalar (array/object) values into a JSON string before transmission whenever a tool's declared JSON Schema leaves the parameter fully untyped (bare {}, no "type", no "items", no "properties") — e.g. create_output_revision.artifacts, append_progress.completed/remaining, list_items.execution_status. The Throughline server then fails json.Unmarshal because it receives a quoted string instead of an array. Confirmed by contrast: fields with an explicit "type":"array" (get_semantic_model.ids; patch_item.acceptance_criterion_resolutions) transmit correctly regardless of content. This is a genuine defect on the calling-environment side, not something a Throughline server code change or the running server's config can fix, and I have no ability to restart/rebuild the currently-connected legacy MCP server mid-session (that lifecycle work is WR-06/07/08).

Practical impact discovered while closing WR-01: I mistakenly called define_expected_output (required:true, ordinal 1) before hitting this wall; there is no tool to remove or un-require an expected_output once created (define_expected_output errors with a UNIQUE constraint on a repeat ordinal, and there is no analogous withdraw/cancel tool). create_output_revision cannot be completed because its required "artifacts" field is untyped and thus unusable, so this expected_output can never be satisfied, which now permanently blocks WR-01's review->done transition (expected_outputs_satisfied), which in turn blocks claim_item on WR-02 (hard_dependencies_satisfied requires WR-01 == done).

Acceptance criteria for WR-01 were separately and successfully resolved via patch_item.acceptance_criterion_resolutions (a properly typed array field), so the actual deliverable (docs/product/workspace-routing-spec.md) is verified complete; only the expected-output gate is stuck.

Recommendation for future work in this objective: avoid define_expected_output/create_output_revision/add_output_requirement for work items unless an output profile's "artifacts" acceptance can be satisfied through a typed-field path; prefer patch_item.acceptance_criterion_resolutions and attach_artifact, both of which are typed and work correctly.
